notes: The location is one room-sized space below stairs, so it is one room: the housekeeper's room, half office and half bedroom, where the keys hang, the accounts are kept and the player's own box stands at the foot of the bed. The player will want to look at the key board, the account book and the box, because those are what the Major turns out and what leaves on the cart.

rooms.name: the housekeeper's room
rooms.description: A low room off the servants' passage, half office and half bedchamber: a deal desk under the one barred window, a narrow iron bed against the far wall, and a key board of brass hooks beside the door where every lock in the house hangs in rows. The window looks at ground level onto the snow of the kitchen yard, so the light comes in grey and comes in low. The small iron stove in the corner takes the chill off and no more. It smells of blacklead, lavender from the linen cupboard, and the damp that lives in the wall behind the bed.

objects.name: the key board
objects.description: Brass hooks in six rows, each labelled in the old housekeeper's hand: cellar, plate, linen, study, the guest rooms by name. The study hook is polished brighter than the rest, and there is one hook at the end with no label and no key.

objects.name: the account book
objects.description: A long ruled ledger of candles, coals, soap and wages, kept to the farthing. The last page in the old housekeeper's hand stops mid-week, and the tallow column for that week was never totted.

objects.name: your box
objects.description: A wooden travelling box with iron corners and your initials painted on the lid, standing at the foot of the bed where it was set down the day you came. The hasp is good, but the lock is the kind any gentleman's penknife could lift.

objects.name: the deal desk
objects.description: A plain desk scrubbed white, with a pen tray, a blotter and a shallow well for the ink. Someone before you has scored a tally in the near edge, five strokes and a bar, and not gone on with it.

objects.name: the iron bed
objects.description: A narrow bedstead with a horsehair mattress and two grey blankets folded to the hospital corner. The wall behind it is stained with damp in the shape of a county nobody can name.

objects.name: the barred window
objects.description: Four iron bars and a sill at the level of the yard, so you see boots before you see faces. The snow outside is trodden to the coal-hole and no further.

objects.name: the stove
objects.description: A small iron stove with a mica door and a kettle that lives on top of it. The ash drawer below has been emptied so often the catch is worn to a nub.

objects.name: the old housekeeper's bonnet
objects.description: A black straw bonnet still on its peg behind the door, the ribbons faded brown. Nobody told you whether Mrs. Dacre died or left, and nobody has asked for it.
